newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ROTTERDAM PORT TURNOVER HITS RECORD IN FIRST HALF.
newsitem.headline: ROTTERDAM PORT TURNOVER HITS RECORD IN FIRST HALF.

text.p: The port of Rotterdam said on
Tuesday first half 1997 turnover was a record 155 million
tonnes, 6.6 percent up on the same 1996 period.
Major growth sectors were oil products (up 37.9 percent),
But incoming agribulk was dropped 5.8 percent and crude oil
Total incoming traffic anounted to 121 million tonnes and
outgoing 33.5 million tonnes against last year's 114 and 31
Container traffic was boosted by increased ferry traffic as
a result of competition from the Channel Tunnel and continuing
high levels of trade between the UK and continental Europe.
A sharp increase in demand for coal from German power
stations helped coal shipments to rise substantially.
Exports of scrap metal were boosted by a shift in Far East
demand to the continent from the United States due to the high
dollar. The decline in agribulk was expained by less global
trade in grains as a result of bad harvests, the port said.
Crude oil throughput fell due to existing stocks.
